palette.notes: Not digital pixel art: grid-paper drawings with markers, filmed with a phone. Measured palette_size 1 is a miss on camera footage. Each drawing uses a few marker colours plus black outline.

lighting: Natural daylight on paper and on a selfie; no designed lighting.
silhouette: Classic simple icons on graph paper (Nyan Cat, ice cream, cupcake, pizza, dolphin, a seal, a bunny), each with a thick black outline.

motion.timing: Slideshow of photos with a selfie intro; code reads 172 changes, 16.92/s, on 1s, but that is camera footage and cuts, not drawing frames. Roughly one drawing every 0.85 s on the sheet.

texture: Hand-drawn 'pixel art' on squared paper with markers: visible grid lines, uneven fills, paper texture. Not pixel art in the digital sense.
camera: Selfie video for the hook, then flat top-down phone photos of each page, some with markers in shot.

acting.enters: The creator appears first as a selfie (talking-head hook), then cuts to the drawings.
acting.acts: No animated character; a slideshow of finished drawings with an on-screen caption.
acting.exits: The creator leaves after the first ~2.5 s; drawings follow one by one.

techniques: NOT pixel art: graph-paper marker drawings, filmed
thick black outline around simple cute icons
on-screen text caption over every cut
feel: not pixel art: selfie hook + fast slideshow of cute grid-paper doodles = relatable hobby post
for_fred: Not a pixel-art reference. Only takeaway: a thick dark outline around a simple chunky shape reads at a glance even rough, so keep Fred's silhouette that simple at small scale. Avoid using this for motion or palette.
